preprintSeeds.title: Continuous data assimilation in steady Navier-Stokes equations with unknown viscosity: robust and efficient solvers and fast parameter recovery

summaries.arxiv:2609.02862: This work develops continuous-data-assimilation solvers that recover an unknown viscosity in the steady Navier–Stokes equations from partial flow observations, with quadratic convergence and strong numerical performance even from poor initial guesses.
summaries.10.1103/qy5r-p5b7: This work separates prediction error into model insufficiency, data insufficiency, and generalized aliasing, providing an explanation for double descent and practical guidance for model and experimental design.
summaries.10.1029/2025jh000667: Bayesian inference and uncertainty analysis are used to reconstruct historical Indonesian earthquakes from anecdotal tsunami evidence and assess which conclusions remain robust under explicit modeling assumptions.
summaries.10.1016/j.jcp.2025.114121: Continuous data assimilation turns online model discovery into a finite-dimensional optimization problem, allowing multiple unknown parameters to be updated as observations arrive.
summaries.10.1007/s00348-025-03991-5: This work compares direct pressure-gradient integration with a Helmholtz–Hodge reconstruction method to characterize how measurement errors propagate into pressure fields recovered from image velocimetry.
summaries.10.1088/1361-6420/adc766: Relaxation least-squares and Newton schemes provide a general framework for recovering unknown states and parameters together in dissipative dynamical systems.
summaries.10.1007/s11069-023-06327-w: Field evidence from imbricated beachrock near the Java trench is used to distinguish tsunami and storm-wave impacts and examine implications for megathrust earthquakes.
summaries.10.1093/gji/ggae044: Bayesian inference compares observations from the 1820 Flores Sea tsunami with a large ensemble of simulations to estimate the most plausible earthquake source and quantify uncertainty.
summaries.10.1103/physrevfluids.9.054602: A complex forcing mechanism in turbulent flow can be reconstructed from partial observations containing fewer than ten percent of the modes used to describe the full system.
